**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that MYH9 and PJVK function in entirely separate, non-interacting cellular pathways within the cochlea, or identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in both MYH9 (dominant-negative) and PJVK (loss-of-function) who do not exhibit hearing impairment. _(variant: Presence of a homozygous pathogenic loss-of-function variant in MYH9 in the gnomAD database at an allele frequency > 0.001.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of MYH9 in distinct modes of inheritance for hearing loss could inform therapeutic strategies targeting cochlear hair cell mechanotransduction, potentially benefiting patients with either AR or AD forms of hearing loss associated with MYH9 dysfunction.
